get.summary: Get or create a participant's assignment.
get.description:
Gets or creates an arm assignment for a participant. The behavior depends on the experiment type:

    - Preassigned A/B experiments: returns the assignment if one exists. `create_if_none` is ignored.
    - Online A/B and Multi-armed Bandit experiments: returns the existing assignment, or creates one
      when `create_if_none` is true.
    - Contextual Multi-armed Bandit (CMAB) experiments: returns the assignment if one exists. To create
      a new assignment, use the `assign_cmab` endpoint, which accepts the required context values.

post.summary: Record a bandit arm outcome for a participant.
post.description:
Records the outcome for a participant's assigned arm and returns the updated arm parameters.

    Use this in push integrations to report each outcome as it happens. Applies only to MAB or
    CMAB experiments using push-based integrations.

    Prerequisites:
    - The experiment must record outcomes through this API. Experiments of type `mab_online_dwh`
      use the pull integration, where Evidential reads outcomes from a connected data warehouse,
      and they reject this call.
    - The participant must already have an assignment. Create one with the GET assignment endpoint
      first.
    - The participant must not already have a recorded outcome. Use the GET assignment endpoint to
      check whether an outcome is already recorded.

    The endpoint returns a 422 error if a prerequisite is not met.

CMABContextInputRequest.title: CMABContextInputRequest
CMABContextInputRequest.description:
Request body for creating a CMAB assignment or running a CMAB experiment analysis.

When you submit context values for a CMAB experiment, these rules apply:
1. Provide one value for every context defined on the experiment.
2. Each context_input must reference a valid context_id defined on the experiment.
3. The order does not matter. Values are matched to contexts by context_id, not by position.
4. context_inputs may be null only when you retrieve an existing assignment.

Example:
    If an experiment defines contexts with IDs ["ctx_1", "ctx_2"], your request must include
    both context_ids in the context_inputs list, in any order.

ExperimentState.description:
Experiment lifecycle states.

Experiments are born in to the ASSIGNED state. The abandon_experiment and commit_experiment APIs transition them to

Filter.title: Filter
Filter.description:
Defines criteria for filtering rows by value.

### Examples

| Relation | Value             | Logical result                                    |
|----------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| INCLUDES | [None]            | Match when `x IS NULL`                            |
| INCLUDES | ["a"]             | Match when `x IN ("a")`                           |
| INCLUDES | ["a", None]       | Match when `x IS NULL OR x IN ("a")`              |
| INCLUDES | ["a", "b"]        | Match when `x IN ("a", "b")`                      |
| EXCLUDES | [None]            | Match `x IS NOT NULL`                             |
| EXCLUDES | ["a", None]       | Match `x IS NOT NULL AND x NOT IN ("a")`          |
| EXCLUDES | ["a", "b"]        | Match `x IS NULL OR (x NOT IN ("a", "b"))`        |
| BETWEEN  | [20, 30]          | Match `20 <= x <= 30`                             |
| BETWEEN  | [20, 30, None]    | Match `20 <= x <= 30` or `x IS NULL`              |
| BETWEEN  | [None, 30]        | Match `x <= 30`                                   |
| BETWEEN  | [20, None]        | Match `x >= 20`                                   |
| BETWEEN  | [None, 30, None]  | Match `x <= 30` or `x IS NULL`                    |

String comparisons are case-sensitive.

### BETWEEN ranges

BETWEEN applies to numeric, DATE, DATETIME and TIMESTAMP fields. Both bounds are inclusive.

The value has 2 or 3 items:
- The first 2 items are the lower and upper bounds. Either bound can be None for an open-ended range, but not both.
- An optional 3rd item, which must be None, also matches null values.

Without the 3rd item, null values never match.

### Handling of DATE, DATETIME and TIMESTAMP values

DATE, DATETIME or TIMESTAMP-type columns support INCLUDES/EXCLUDES/BETWEEN, similar to numerics.

Values must be expressed as ISO8601 datetime strings compatible with Python's datetime.fromisoformat()
(https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#dt.datetime.fromisoformat).

If a timezone is provided, it must be UTC.

sufficient_n.description: Whether there are enough available participants to sample to reach target_n.

target_possible.title: Target Possible
target_possible.description: When the sample size is too small to reach the desired metric_target, this is the target that is possible given available_n, in the improvement (positive) direction from the baseline. It is the absolute counterpart of pct_change_possible. None when the sample size is large enough to detect the desired change, or (for BINARY metrics) when no value above the baseline is a large enough change to reach the requested power.

pct_change_possible.title: Pct Change Possible
pct_change_possible.description: When the sample size is too small to reach the desired metric_pct_change, this is the percent change that is possible given available_n. It is the relative counterpart of target_possible. None whenever target_possible is None.

target_possible_lower.title: Target Possible Lower
target_possible_lower.description: The detectable metric value below the baseline. (target_possible is the metric value above the baseline.) Both detectable metric values above and below the baseline use the chosen confidence and power, and are always reported together, regardless of the direction of the requested change. For numeric metrics, this is the same distance below the baseline as target_possible is above it. However, for binary metrics, an increase and a decrease that are equally detectable can sit at different distances from the baseline. None when the sample size is large enough to detect the desired change, or (for BINARY metrics) when no value below the baseline is a large enough change to reach the requested power.

pct_change_possible_lower.title: Pct Change Possible Lower
pct_change_possible_lower.description: The relative counterpart of target_possible_lower, as a percent change from the baseline (negative for a decrease). A value of -0.10 means a 10% decrease. None whenever target_possible_lower is None.

pct_change_with_desired_n.title: Pct Change With Desired N
pct_change_with_desired_n.description: The minimum detectable effect (MDE) achievable for the desired sample size at the chosen confidence and power, reported in the direction of the requested change (negative when the requested change is a decrease from the baseline). Present only when design_spec.desired_n or design_spec.desired_n_clusters is set (frequentist design specs). When desired_n_clusters is set, the desired sample size is desired_n_clusters times this metric's avg_cluster_size.

mde_curve.title: Mde Curve
mde_curve.description: The MDE for each requested sample size, in the same order as design_spec.desired_ns (or desired_ns_clusters, which takes precedence). Present only when one of those is set. Each point is computed best-effort: a size where the calculation fails yields a null pct_change instead of failing the request.

Relation.title: Relation
Relation.description:
Defines operators for filtering values.

INCLUDES matches when the value matches any of the provided values, including null if explicitly
specified. This is equivalent to NOT(EXCLUDES(values)).

EXCLUDES matches when the value does not match any of the provided values, including null if
explicitly specified. If null is not explicitly excluded, we include nulls in the result.

BETWEEN matches when the value is between the two provided bounds (inclusive). Either bound can be
null for an open-ended range. A null value matches only if a 3rd value of null is provided. BETWEEN
applies to numeric, date and timestamp values.

tags.name: Experiment Integration
tags.description:
## Integrate experiments into your application using Evidential.

Evidential's Experiments API allows you to integrate Evidential experiments with your application or workflows using
a REST API.

Tip: This documentation is interactive. Click the "Authorize" button at the top of the page to set your data source
API key. Create an API key in [Evidential](https://app.evidential.dev/).

Evidential supports many experimentation and integration strategies. The specific endpoints you will integrate with
depend on the type of experiment you are running and your integration strategy.

Outcomes reach Evidential in one of two ways, and the experiment type determines which:

- Push: your application reports each outcome by calling the outcome endpoint.
- Pull: Evidential reads outcomes from your data source, and your application reports none.

Assignment works the same way for every experiment type. Your application asks Evidential which arm a participant
belongs to, so push and pull describe outcomes only.

Preassigned A/B experiments (pull) — assignments are created when the experiment is designed, before the experiment
starts:

- `GET /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}/assignments` lists all assignments.
- `GET /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}/assignments/csv` exports all assignments as CSV.
- `GET /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}/assignments/{participant_id}` looks up one participant's assignment. For
  applications that can't store assignments separately, your application can call this method at runtime.

Online A/B experiments (pull) — assignments are created as participants arrive:

- `GET /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}/assignments/{participant_id}` gets or creates a participant's assignment.
- `POST /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}/assignments/{participant_id}/assign_with_filters`
  gets or creates an assignment when the experiment uses server-side filtering.

Multi-armed Bandit (MAB) experiments (push) — assignments are created as participants arrive, and you report each
outcome:

- `GET /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}/assignments/{participant_id}` gets or creates a participant's assignment.
- `POST /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}/assignments/{participant_id}/outcome`
  records the outcome for a participant's arm.

A MAB experiment whose outcome column is bound to a table in your data source (`mab_online_dwh`) uses pull instead.
Your application calls the assignment endpoint alone, and Evidential reads each outcome from that column.

Contextual Multi-armed Bandit (CMAB) experiments (push) — assignments use context values you supply, and you report
each outcome:

- `POST /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}/assignments/{participant_id}/assign_cmab`
  gets or creates a participant's assignment from the context values you supply.
- `POST /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}/assignments/{participant_id}/outcome`
  records the outcome for a participant's arm.

These endpoints can be used to synchronize experiment state with your workflows:

- `GET /v1/experiments` lists experiments on the data source.
- `GET /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}` gets an experiment's design and assignment specs.

Authentication: Every method in this API requires the `X-API-Key` request header containing your data source API
key. Manage your keys under Settings, in the Data Sources section.

Error handling: Branch on the HTTP status code, not on the text of the error message. Status codes are stable, but
message text may change. 2xx codes indicate success. 4xx codes usually indicate a problem with your request. 5xx codes
indicate a server-side error and may be retried.

Retries: Retry only transient failures, meaning network errors and 5xx responses. Use exponential backoff with
jitter, and cap the number of attempts. Do not retry 4xx responses. They will fail again until you change the request
or until the experiment, data source, or assignment state changes. Assignment requests are safe to retry, because they
return the existing assignment when one was already created.
